entities.name: PMID:10738086
observations: Single irradiation of isolated human PBMCs at 0.1–0.5 Gy reduced adhesion of viable cells to activated murine endothelioma cells to about 70% of control at 4 hours under shear; loss of L-selectin was implicated.
The study describes the response as selective, but does not provide detailed PBMC lineage-by-lineage selectivity analysis.

entities.name: PMID:12020443
observations: Irradiation of TNF-α-activated human EA.hy.926 endothelial monolayers at 0.3–0.6 Gy reduced static and dynamic PBMC adhesion at 4 and 24 hours, but adhesion increased at 12 hours.
The endothelial response implicated altered E-selectin behavior; ICAM-1 was not induced or modulated at doses up to 5 Gy.

entities.name: PMID:12194755
observations: Endothelial irradiation produced a PBMC adhesion minimum at 0.3–0.7 Gy; neutralizing TGF-β1 nearly restored adhesion and E-selectin was downregulated.
The findings support an anti-adhesive endothelial response rather than nonspecific cytotoxicity.

entities.name: PMID:15057429
observations: In TNF-α-stimulated EA.hy.926 cells exposed to 0.3–3 Gy, PBMC adhesion decreased at 4 and 24 hours but increased by up to 30% at 12 hours.
The effect is therefore biphasic and time-dependent.

entities.name: PMID:26051282
observations: At 0.5 Gy, PBMC adhesion decreased in TNF-α-stimulated EA.hy.926 cells and primary human dermal microvascular endothelial cells.
ROS scavenging or Nrf2 activation diminished the reduction, implicating redox signaling.

entities.name: Low-dose RT reduces PBMC adhesion
observations: Across multiple in-vitro models, approximately 0.1–0.7 Gy commonly reduced PBMC adhesion to activated endothelium at selected time points, with effects ranging from modest reduction to roughly 25–70% of control.
Evidence supports reduced adhesion behavior, but not definitive selective depletion of a particular PBMC lineage.
